decision_summary: spec.md determines processing order only by strict priority; it is silent on the relative order of jobs sharing a priority, and probes.json contains several equal-priority groups, so more than one spec-conforming output is possible on those probes. The required evidence E-B is an item-level comparison over probes.json against an implementation authored strictly from spec.md by someone with no access to reference.py and no analysis derived from it. This session observed reference.py during observe-package and therefore cannot supply that clean-room implementation at full strength; a fresh, isolated child that receives only spec.md and probes.json can. Hence CREATE.

assigned_distinctions.role: Independently surface every behavior spec.md leaves undetermined on the probes, by forcing a concrete implementation choice at each open point.
Produce a runnable next_order.py from spec.md alone plus per-probe outputs, enabling the root's mechanical item-level comparison against reference.py.

expected_child_contribution.expected_evidence: child-result.json.undetermined_behaviors — behaviors spec.md does not determine, rediscovered without reference exposure.
child/next_order.py and child-result.json.per_probe_outputs — the clean-room implementation and its outputs for the root to compare against reference.py.

integration_rule_reference: child/integration-plan.json (method: clean_room_comparison; verdict UNDERDETERMINED on any per-probe divergence, else SUFFICIENT; findings derived from divergent probe indices and the child's reported undetermined behaviors).
notes: The parent commits to the integration rule now; the root executes it mechanically over the returned child evidence and never solves the task itself. Final result.json is produced by the root at verify-trial-child, not by this session.
